+<p dir="auto">When contributing, post comments and discuss changes you wish to make via Issues.</p>
+<p dir="auto">Feel free to propose changes by creating Pull Requests. If you don't have write access, editing a file will create a Fork of this project for you to save your proposed changes to. Submitting a change to a file will write it to a new Branch in your Fork, so you can send a Pull Request.</p>
+<p dir="auto">If this is your first time contributing on GitHub, don't worry! Let us know if you have any questions.</p>

+<p dir="auto">Lorsque vous contribuez, veuillez également publier des commentaires et discuter des modifications que vous souhaitez apporter par l'entremise des enjeux (Issues).</p>
+<p dir="auto">N'hésitez pas à proposer des modifications en créant des demandes de tirage (Pull Requests). Si vous n'avez pas accès au mode de rédaction, la modification d'un fichier créera une copie (Fork) de ce projet afin que vous puissiez enregistrer les modifications que vous proposez. Le fait de proposer une modification à un fichier l'écrira dans une nouvelle branche dans votre copie (Fork), de sorte que vous puissiez envoyer une demande de tirage (Pull Request).</p>
+<p dir="auto">Si c'est la première fois que vous contribuez à GitHub, ne vous en faites pas! Faites-nous part de vos questions.</p>

+<p dir="auto">This project will host the minimum guardrails as part of the GC Cloud Operationalization Framework for Oracle. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is an approved Cloud Service Provider.</p>
+<p dir="auto">The purpose of the guardrails is to ensure that departments and agencies are implementing a preliminary baseline set of controls within their cloud-based environments.</p>
+<p dir="auto">These minimum guardrails are to be implemented within the GC-specified initial period (e.g. 30 days) upon receipt of an enrollment under the GC Cloud Services Framework Agreement.</p>
+<p dir="auto">This <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/Guardrails%20Implementation%20Guidance%20for%20Oracle%20Cloud%20-%20EN%20(Dec%202020).pdf">document</a> provides a brief overview of each applicable guardrail and instructions on how to implement them when using OCI.</p>
+<p dir="auto">For a quicker way to deploy a secure environment fit for the Guardrails on OCI, be sure to use the OCI Landing Zone accelerator.
+See <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/tree/main/oci-cis-landingzone-quickstart">OCI Landing Zone Quickstart</a></p>
+<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/OCI%20Cloud%20Guardrails%20-%20EN.pdf">OCI Prowler</a> is a command-line tool that can be used to validate the guardrails implementation.</p>

+<p dir="auto">Ce projet hébergera les garde-corps minimums dans le cadre de l’opérationnalisation de l’informatique en nuage du GC pour Oracle. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) est un fournisseur de services cloud approuvé.</p>
+<p dir="auto">Le but des garde-corps est de garantir que les ministères et organismes mettent en œuvre un ensemble de base de contrôle préliminaire dans leurs environnements cloud.
+Ces garde-corps minimaux doivent être mis en œuvre au cours de la période initiale spécifiée par le GC (par exemple, 30 jours) à la réception d'une inscription en vertu de l'Accord-cadre des services cloud du GC.</p>
+<p dir="auto">Ce <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/Guardrails%20Implementation%20Guidance%20for%20Oracle%20Cloud%20-%20FR%20(Dec%202020).pdf">document</a> fournit un bref aperçu de chaque garde-corps applicable et des instructions sur la façon de les mettre en œuvre lors de l'utilisation d'OCI.</p>
+<p dir="auto">Pour un moyen plus rapide de déployer un environnement sécurisé adapté aux garde-corps sur OCI, assurez-vous d'utiliser l'accélérateur OCI Landing Zone.
+Voir <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/tree/main/oci-cis-landingzone-quickstart">Démarrage rapide de la zone d'atterrissage OCI</a></p>
+<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/OCI%20Cloud%20Guardrails%20-%20FR.pdf">OCI Prowler</a> est un outil de ligne de commande qui peut être utilisé pour valider l’implémentation des garde-corps.</p>

You are Worker B. Your job is to gather content judgments about the GitHub repository `tracker` at `https://github.com/canada-ca/tracker`.

You must read files and discussions, then write your findings to `/workspace/manual_tracker.json` as a JSON object with exactly these keys and allowed values.

Keys to determine:
1. `bilingual`: Read the README (or at least the first few hundred lines). Does it contain meaningful content in both English and French? Look for French words/phrases, French section headers, or a clear French translation. Allowed: `Yes`/`No`/`Unknown`.
2. `readme_clarity`: Read the README. Does it clearly explain what the project is, who it's for, and how to use it? `Poor`/`Fair`/`Good`/`Unknown`.
3. `security_policy`: Check for `SECURITY.md` in root, `.github/`, and `docs/`. If not found, write `Missing`. If found, read it. If it contains real responsible disclosure instructions (contact info, how to report, PGP key, etc.), write `Present`. If it exists but is just a placeholder or links without real instructions, write `Incomplete`. Allowed: `Present`/`Incomplete`/`Missing`/`Unknown`.
4. `issue_response_quality`: Look at the 5 most recently updated open issues (API `issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc`, filter out PRs). For each, check if anyone other than the original reporter commented within the last 6 months (from 2026-07-13). If at least one issue has such a comment, write `Active`. If none, write `Stale`. If there are no open issues, write `No Issues`. Allowed: `Active`/`Stale`/`No Issues`/`Unknown`.
5. `release_notes_quality`: Check the Releases page (API `releases` or HTML). If no releases, write `No Releases`. If releases exist, check the latest few. If the description actually explains what changed (e.g., bullet points, changelog), write `Detailed`. If it's just a version number or tag with no description, write `Version-only`. Allowed: `Detailed`/`Version-only`/`No Releases`/`Unknown`.

IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use ONLY the exact allowed values for each column.
- If you cannot determine a value, write exactly `Unknown`.
- Never derive a column from another `Unknown` column.
- Prefer public HTML page scraping over GitHub API where possible to avoid rate limits. If using API, add `sleep 1` between requests.
- Use the Bash tool with curl and jq for API calls. For HTML scraping, use curl.
- Write the final JSON to `/workspace/manual_tracker.json`.

Return the content of the JSON file you wrote in your final message.

display.text:
# Tracker

This project tracks Government of Canada domains for adherence to digital security best practices and federal requirements.

## Application structure

In pursuit of a vision of [Government as a Platform](https://medium.com/digitalhks/a-working-definition-of-government-as-a-platform-1fa6ff2f8e8d), the TBS [Directive on Service and Digital](https://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32601) states that developers should ["Validate your API design by consuming it"](https://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32604#claB.2.2.4) and ["Use microservices built around business capabilities"](https://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32602#claA.2.3.10.2). Supporting this vision and taking this guidance to heart has meant that the core of the Tracker system is an API/consumer pair resulting in a minimalist microservices architecture.

The Directive also says ["Design for cloud mobility"](https://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32602#claA.2.3.11.3), ["Use distributed architectures"](https://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32602#claA.2.3.12.4), ["Run applications in containers"](https://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32602#claA.2.3.10.4) and to use ["open source software first"](https://www.tbs-sct.gc.ca/pol/doc-eng.aspx?id=32602#claA.2.3.8.1).
The technology at the intersection of these four directives is [Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/), which is used as a cloud agnostic platform to deploy the services that make up the Tracker system.

## Repo Structure

As is common with microservices projects, this repository is organized in the [monorepo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monorepo) style with the various services/components separated into their own folders.

```
.
├── api
├── ci
├── clients
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── frontend
├── guidance
├── Makefile
├── README.md
├── scripts
├── SECURITY.md
└── services
```

The [ci](ci/README.md) folder contains an image used in the CI process, but the main event is the next three folders:

The [frontend](frontend/README.md) and [api](api/README.md) folders contain the two main parts of the application.

The [k8s](k8s/README.md) folder contain the Kubernetes configurations needed to continuously deploy the tracker on the cloud provider of your choice.

The clients folder contains API clients offered as an alternative to Tracker's web frontend. Only a [Python client](clients/python/README.md) is available at this time.

The services folder contains smaller services dedicated to scanning or account creation.

The scripts folder is a dumping ground for various utility scripts and codemods.

## Running it locally

Running Tracker locally takes a few commands and a lot of RAM. See the instructions in the [k8s folder](k8s/README.md)

## Deploying to the cloud

Assuming a connection to the target cluster has been established, navigate to the root of the repository.

```
$ make credentials
```

```
$ make platform env=<your cloud platform (gke/aks)>
```

```
$ make secrets env=<gke or aks>
```

```
$ make platform env=<gke or aks>
```

```
$ make app env=<gke or aks>
```

Tracker is now deployed. To add continuous deployment functionality via [Flux](https://fluxcd.io/) (this will ensure the Tracker deployment stays up to date with all the latest changes), follow the instructions listed below.

### NOTE: Steps 1) and 2) are only required if the Tracker deployment should write back to this repository, updating image tags as necessary.

1. Create SSH key:

```
ssh-keygen -q -N "" -C "flux-read-write" -f ./k8s/clusters/auto-image-update/bases/creds/identity
```

```
ssh-keygen github.com > ./k8s/clusters/auto-image-update/bases/creds/known_hosts
```

2. [Add key to repository](https://github.com/canada-ca/tracker/settings/keys/new)

3. Finally, run:

```
$ make deploy env=<gke or aks>
```

Tracker is now fully deployed, with continuous deployment functionality provided by Flux!
